---
title: "Building a Windows DFIR box"
subtitle: "Build a repeatable Windows workstation for analyzing evidence that has already been collected."
---

## What we're building

- A Windows analysis machine, not an evidence acquisition machine.
- Evidence is already collected; memory acquisition is handled separately (Magnet in our workflow).

The box takes collected artifacts (triage collections, event logs, registry hives, disk images, memory images) and produces analysis output: parsed CSVs, timelines, notes. It never touches the client's systems.

This is an opinionated build. Each choice below has alternatives; these are the ones that have worked.

| | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | Windows Server 2025, Desktop Experience | Stable Long-Term Servicing Channel release; Microsoft Defender Antivirus is a feature you can remove; no TPM requirement |
| Hypervisor | VMware Workstation Pro | Independent non-persistent disks reset on power-off; Shared Folders, one of them read-only, keep case data outside the VM |
| Install | An unattend file | The same Windows build every time, with the settings below already applied |
| Settings | UAC off, Defender removed, long paths on, extensions and hidden files shown | Analysis tools run without friction on a machine that is thrown away |
| Tools | Chocolatey, plus a few direct downloads; WSL 1 for Linux tools | One command line installs most of the list, and records versions |

## Disposable/nonpersistent virtual machine

- Return the machine to a known state.
- Keep case data and analysis output separate from what gets reset.

**Why disposable.** Analysis tools open hostile files. Each case starts from the same known-good image, nothing carries over from the previous client, and "what version of the tool did we use" has one answer.

### VMware Workstation Pro

Workstation Pro has been free for commercial, educational and personal use since November 2024 ([Broadcom](https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/368667/download-and-license-vmware-desktop-hypervisor.html)); download it from the Broadcom support portal.

| | Lives where | On reset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows, settings, installed tools | System disk, **independent non-persistent** | Discarded at power-off |
| Temporary files, caches, tool state | System disk | Discarded at power-off |
| Evidence | Host folder, shared **read-only** | Kept; the VM cannot change it |
| Analysis output, tool logs, notes | Host folder, shared read-write | Kept |

**Non-persistent system disk.** Build the VM with a normal disk, install and configure everything, shut it down, then in **VM Settings → Hard Disk → Advanced** set the disk to *Independent* and *Nonpersistent*. From then on, changes are discarded when you power off the VM or restore a snapshot, and the disk is in the same state every time it starts ([VMware Workstation Pro documentation](https://docs.vmware.com/en/VMware-Workstation-Pro/17/com.vmware.ws.using.doc/GUID-A6792F54-2734-4AF4-9473-C8B9AD8321AF.html)). A restart inside Windows is not a power-off; shut down, and power the VM off. To update the image, switch the disk back to persistent, update, and switch it back.

**Shared Folders.** In **VM Settings → Options → Shared Folders**, add two host folders: `Evidence` with the **Read-only** attribute, so the VM can view and copy files but cannot add, change or remove them, and `Cases` read-write for output. With VMware Tools installed, they appear in Windows at `\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\`. Host file permissions still apply.

**Verify it.** Write a test file to `Cases`, try (and fail) to write one to `Evidence`, power off, power on, and confirm the `Cases` file is still there and a file you left on the desktop is gone.

## Automating the build

- Decide on the Windows image and tool list.
- Make setup repeatable rather than configuring it by hand each time.

### Windows Server 2025

Use the Desktop Experience installation option; the analysis tools need a desktop. Microsoft's [Evaluation Center](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/evalcenter/download-windows-server-2025) has a 180-day evaluation, which must be activated online within its first 10 days or it shuts down; activate it during the build, while the VM has a network. A licensed image is the alternative. Why Server rather than Windows 11:

- **Stable.** Long-Term Servicing Channel: no feature updates rearranging the system between cases.
- **Defender is a feature.** On Windows Server, Microsoft Defender Antivirus is installed as a Windows feature, `Windows-Defender`, so it can be removed cleanly instead of fought with ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/microsoft-defender-antivirus-windows-server-configure)).
- **No TPM requirement.** Microsoft lists a TPM as "required only for certain features," such as BitLocker ([hardware requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/get-started/hardware-requirements)), so the VM needs no virtual TPM, and no encryption of the VM that a virtual TPM brings with it in Workstation.

### Unattended install

An unattend file (`autounattend.xml`) answers every question Windows Setup asks and can apply settings and run scripts. Build one with [Christoph Schneegans' unattend generator](https://schneegans.de/windows/unattend-generator/). Settings to choose for this box:

| Generator setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| A local administrator account | No Microsoft account; one known login |
| Disable User Account Control (UAC) | See [UAC](#uac) below |
| Enable long paths | Deep paths inside collections otherwise fail |
| Always show file extensions; show all files | `invoice.pdf.exe` and hidden files are visible |
| Do not update Last Access Time stamp | Reading a file on the box does not change its last access time |
| Set your time zone explicitly: (UTC) Coordinated Universal Time | See [Clock](#clock) below |
| Disable SmartScreen | Tools downloaded during the build are not blocked |
| Remove bloatware | Fewer distractions and background updates |
| FirstLogon scripts | Install Chocolatey and the tools ([below](#tools-for-analysis)) |

The generator is written for Windows 10 and 11, and its files work for Windows Server 2025 once you make two choices by hand:

- **Product key.** Choose *Enter another product key* and enter your own key, or the generic key for the edition from Microsoft's [KMS client product keys](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/get-started/kms-client-activation-keys) (Windows Server 2025 Standard: `TVRH6-WHNXV-R9WG3-9XRFY-MY832`). The generic key picks the edition; it does not activate Windows.
- **Image.** Choose *Select image with this name* or *Select image with this index*, and pick a Desktop Experience image. To list the images on the ISO, mount it and run `Get-WindowsImage -ImagePath D:\sources\install.wim` in an elevated PowerShell (D: being the mounted ISO).

Generate the file again when you change the build, rather than editing the XML by hand.

#### Using the file

Windows Setup looks for a file named `Autounattend.xml` at the root of removable media, including read-only media such as a DVD or a mounted ISO ([Windows Setup Automation Overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/windows-setup-automation-overview)). The generator's download already has that name. There are two ways to give it to Setup in a VM:

- **A second, small ISO** that holds only `autounattend.xml`, attached as a second CD/DVD drive. The Windows ISO stays untouched, and you can swap answer files without rebuilding anything.
- **A customized Windows ISO** with `autounattend.xml` added at its root. One ISO to attach, and it works the same on a physical machine.

Both need `oscdimg.exe`, which comes with the [Windows ADK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/get-started/adk-install) (install only the *Deployment Tools* feature).

```powershell
# Where the ADK installs oscdimg
$Oscdimg = 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Assessment and Deployment Kit\Deployment Tools\amd64\Oscdimg\oscdimg.exe'

# A folder holding only the answer file, made into a small ISO
New-Item -Path C:\Build\Answer -ItemType Directory -Force
Copy-Item -Path "$HOME\Downloads\autounattend.xml" -Destination C:\Build\Answer
& $Oscdimg -u2 -udfver102 C:\Build\Answer C:\Build\autounattend.iso
```

#### Customizing the Windows ISO

Copy the contents of the Windows ISO to a folder, add the answer file at its root, and build a new bootable ISO. `efisys_noprompt.bin` is the UEFI boot file that skips "Press any key to boot from CD or DVD," so the install runs with no one at the keyboard; use `efisys.bin` to keep the prompt. Images over 4.5 GB need a boot order file that puts the boot files first ([Oscdimg command-line options](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/oscdimg-command-line-options)); the script writes one from the `boot` and `efi` folders.

```powershell
# Paths without spaces: oscdimg's -bootdata and -yo options do not accept them
$IsoPath = 'C:\Build\Server2025.iso'
$Build = 'C:\Build\Server2025'

# Copy everything off the Windows ISO
$Drive = (Mount-DiskImage -ImagePath $IsoPath -PassThru | Get-Volume).DriveLetter
New-Item -Path $Build -ItemType Directory -Force
Copy-Item -Path "${Drive}:\*" -Destination $Build -Recurse
Dismount-DiskImage -ImagePath $IsoPath

# Add the answer file at the root
Copy-Item -Path "$HOME\Downloads\autounattend.xml" -Destination $Build

# Boot order file: the boot files, then boot.wim, as paths relative to the root
$Order = 'C:\Build\BootOrder.txt'
Get-ChildItem -Path "$Build\boot", "$Build\efi" -Recurse -File |
	ForEach-Object { $_.FullName.Substring($Build.Length + 1) } |
	Set-Content -Path $Order -Encoding Ascii
Add-Content -Path $Order -Value 'sources\boot.wim' -Encoding Ascii

# A new ISO that boots on BIOS and UEFI
$BootData = "2#p0,e,b$Build\boot\etfsboot.com#pEF,e,b$Build\efi\microsoft\boot\efisys_noprompt.bin"
& $Oscdimg -m -o -u2 -udfver102 "-bootdata:$BootData" "-yo$Order" $Build C:\Build\Server2025-unattend.iso
```

#### Installing

1. In Workstation, create the VM with **I will install the operating system later**, so VMware's Easy Install does not supply its own answers. Keep the default UEFI firmware.
2. Attach the Windows ISO and the answer-file ISO (or only the customized ISO).
3. Power on. With the generator's disk and account settings, Setup partitions the disk, installs and signs in without asking anything; the FirstLogon scripts run at the first sign-in.
4. Check the result, then remove the ISOs from the VM.

Setup caches the answer file in `C:\Windows\Panther`, with the administrator password and product key in it. Delete it before you make the disk non-persistent, so it is not part of every case:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Windows\Panther -Filter *unattend*.xml | Remove-Item
```

## Configuring Windows for analysis

- Tools that need to run as administrator.
- UAC: normally I don't disable security features, but this is a disposable VM and reducing friction matters.
- Other Windows security settings as decisions specific to this machine, not general recommendations.

These are the settings, and the command for each if you apply it after setup instead of in the unattend file. Run them in an elevated PowerShell.

| Setting | Command |
| --- | --- |
| UAC off | `Set-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System -Name EnableLUA -Value 0`, then restart |
| Remove Microsoft Defender Antivirus | `Uninstall-WindowsFeature -Name Windows-Defender`, then restart (check the name with `Get-WindowsFeature *defender*`) |
| Long paths | `Set-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem -Name LongPathsEnabled -Value 1` |
| Show file extensions | `Set-ItemProperty -Path HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced -Name HideFileExt -Value 0` |
| Show hidden files | Same key: `Hidden` = 1 |
| Show protected system files | Same key: `ShowSuperHidden` = 1 |
| No last-access updates | `fsutil behavior set disablelastaccess 1` |
| Server Manager not at every logon | `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName ServerManager \| Disable-ScheduledTask` |

### UAC {#uac}

With `EnableLUA` = 0, Admin Approval Mode is off and administrators run everything elevated, so tools that need administrator rights simply work. The middle ground is `ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin` = 0: UAC stays on and elevates without prompting, but programs still start unelevated unless asked. See Microsoft's [User Account Control settings and configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/user-account-control/settings-and-configuration).

### Clock {#clock}

Analysis output is easier to read when the screen agrees with it. NTFS stores file times in UTC ([File Times](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/file-times)), and many forensic tools, including Eric Zimmerman's tools and plaso, report UTC, while Windows (Explorer, Event Viewer) shows times in the system's time zone. Either:

- **Use UTC as the system time zone.** Everything on screen is UTC. In the unattend generator, set the time zone explicitly to *(UTC) Coordinated Universal Time*, or run `Set-TimeZone -Id 'UTC'` ([Set-TimeZone](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/set-timezone)).
- **Keep local time and add a second clock set to UTC.** Control Panel → **Date and Time** → **Additional Clocks**: tick *Show this clock*, choose *(UTC) Coordinated Universal Time* and name it `UTC`. Hovering over the taskbar clock shows both.

### Network and updates

Analysis rarely needs the internet; installs and tool updates do. Connect the VM during the build, then keep it off the internet during cases: a host-only network, or none. Hostile files cannot reach out, and the tools stay at the versions in the image. Windows Update in the middle of a case changes the system under the analysis; update the clean image on a schedule instead.

## Tools for analysis

- Select the tools and versions.
- KAPE modules for processing already-collected artifacts.

### Chocolatey and Scoop

[Chocolatey](https://chocolatey.org/install) installs most of the list from one command, which makes the FirstLogon step one line. Its community packages are maintained by volunteers, separately from the tools' authors: check the package page links to the real project before adding it. [Scoop](https://scoop.sh/) is an alternative that installs per user without administrator rights; it has fewer DFIR tools.

```powershell
choco install -y 7zip sysinternals pwsh vscode git python wireshark cyberchef exiftool arsenalimagemounter ericzimmermantools volatility3 autopsy

# Python tools, in a new window so python and pip are on the PATH
pip install -U oletools[full]
```

There is no need to pin versions. The non-persistent disk keeps every tool at the version in the image until you deliberately update it, and Scoop keeps earlier versions side by side when it updates an app (`scoop cleanup` removes them). Record what is installed for the case notes:

```powershell
choco list | Out-File -FilePath "\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\Cases\2026-0142\Notes\Tools.txt"
```

### The tool list

The common Windows tools from DFIR distributions such as [FLARE-VM](https://github.com/mandiant/flare-vm) and the [SIFT Workstation](https://www.sans.org/tools/sift-workstation/), grouped by job.

| Tool | For | Install |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Parsing and timelines** | | |
| [Eric Zimmerman's tools](https://ericzimmerman.github.io/) | Registry, event logs, MFT, LNK, jump lists; Timeline Explorer for the CSVs | `choco install ericzimmermantools`, or his `Get-ZimmermanTools.ps1` |
| [KAPE](https://www.kroll.com/kape) | Running modules over a collection | Download from Kroll after registering; see licensing below |
| [Chainsaw](https://github.com/WithSecureLabs/chainsaw) | Hunting through event logs with Sigma rules | Release zip from GitHub (Chocolatey's `chainsaw` is a different program) |
| [Hayabusa](https://github.com/Yamato-Security/hayabusa) | Event log timelines and Sigma detections | Release zip from GitHub |
| [log2timeline / plaso](https://plaso.readthedocs.io/) | Super timelines | In [WSL](#wsl), from the GIFT PPA as the [plaso documentation](https://plaso.readthedocs.io/en/latest/sources/user/Ubuntu-Packaged-Release.html) describes: `sudo add-apt-repository ppa:gift/stable`, then `sudo apt install plaso-tools` |
| **Disk images and memory** | | |
| [FTK Imager](https://www.exterro.com/digital-forensics-software/ftk-imager) | Mounting and browsing disk images, hashing | Download from Exterro |
| [Arsenal Image Mounter](https://arsenalrecon.com/products/arsenal-image-mounter) | Mounting images as complete disks, so any Windows tool can read them; Free Mode includes temporary write support kept in separate differencing files | `choco install arsenalimagemounter` |
| [Autopsy](https://www.sleuthkit.org/autopsy/) | Disk image analysis | `choco install autopsy` |
| [Volatility 3](https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/volatility3) | Memory images | `choco install volatility3` |
| **Files, documents and network** | | |
| [CyberChef](https://gchq.github.io/CyberChef/) | Decoding, decompressing and converting data; a local copy that works offline | `choco install cyberchef` |
| [ExifTool](https://exiftool.org/) | File metadata | `choco install exiftool` |
| [pestudio](https://www.winitor.com/) | First look at a Windows executable | Download from Winitor (Chocolatey flags its package as possibly broken) |
| [oletools](https://github.com/decalage2/oletools) | Macros and objects in Office documents | `pip install -U oletools[full]` |
| [Wireshark](https://www.wireshark.org/) | Packet captures | `choco install wireshark` |
| **Basics** | | |
| 7-Zip, [Sysinternals](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/), PowerShell 7, Git, Python | Archives, process and file utilities, scripting | In the `choco` line above |
| [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) | Reading scripts, logs, JSON and CSV; editing notes | `choco install vscode` |
| Microsoft Office | Documents, and Excel for the CSVs | If your license covers it |

Also common in those distributions, if your work calls for them: [Notepad++](https://notepad-plus-plus.org/) (`notepadplusplus`), [HxD](https://mh-nexus.de/en/hxd/) (`hxd`), [DB Browser for SQLite](https://sqlitebrowser.org/) (`sqlitebrowser`) and [YARA](https://virustotal.github.io/yara/) (`yara`) from Chocolatey; [RegRipper](https://github.com/keydet89/RegRipper3.0), [capa](https://github.com/mandiant/capa) and [FLOSS](https://github.com/mandiant/flare-floss) from their GitHub releases (their Chocolatey packages are years behind).

Record the version of every tool used for a case in the case notes.

### WSL {#wsl}

The Windows Subsystem for Linux runs Linux command-line tools, such as plaso, next to the Windows tools, on the same files. Windows Server 2025 installs it with `wsl.exe --install` ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install-on-server)).

**Inside VMware Workstation, use WSL 1.** WSL 2 runs Linux in a lightweight virtual machine, so inside this VM it needs nested virtualization: **VM Settings → Processors → Virtualize Intel VT-x/EPT or AMD-V/RVI**. Workstation cannot provide that while the host itself runs Hyper-V or virtualization-based security, which Memory Integrity, Credential Guard, WSL 2 and Docker Desktop on the host all turn on ([Broadcom KB 389469](https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/389469/virtualized-intel-vtxept-is-not-supporte.html)). On a Windows 11 host with virtualization-based security running, Workstation 25.0.1 refused to power on a VM with that option set: "Virtualized Intel VT-x/EPT is not supported on this platform." WSL 1 does not use virtualization, so it works whatever the host runs.

```powershell
# WSL with the WSL 1 component, and no distribution yet; restart afterwards
wsl.exe --install --enable-wsl1 --no-distribution

# After the restart: new distributions use WSL 1, then install Ubuntu
wsl.exe --set-default-version 1
wsl.exe --install --distribution Ubuntu

# The VERSION column should show 1
wsl.exe --list --verbose
```

Install the distribution and its tools during the build, like everything else on the system disk. Windows drives appear in Linux under `/mnt/c` and so on ([WSL commands](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/basic-commands)).

### Processing an existing artifact set with KAPE modules

KAPE has two halves: **targets** collect files from a system, and **modules** run programs against files already collected. For this box only modules apply. Modules are defined in `.mkape` files; the community set is maintained in [KapeFiles](https://github.com/EricZimmerman/KapeFiles), which includes the compound module `!EZParser` (runs Eric Zimmerman's parsers over a collection).

```powershell
# Module source is a collection that already exists; output goes to case storage.
.\kape.exe --msource "\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\Evidence\2026-0142\C" --mdest "\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\Cases\2026-0142\Output\EZParser" --module !EZParser
```

Check the switches against `kape.exe --help` and the [KAPE documentation](https://ericzimmerman.github.io/KapeDocs/) for the version you install.

**Licensing.** KAPE is free for CRT members. Commercial use, such as paid engagements, requires an enterprise license from Kroll: [KAPE license agreement](https://www.kroll.com/en/kape-license-agreement).

## Using and resetting the box

- Run tools against existing artifacts.
- Retain the results and relevant logs.
- Verify the environment and reset it for the next case.

A per-case checklist:

1. Power on from the non-persistent image. Confirm `\\vmware-host\Shared Folders\Evidence` is read-only and `Cases` is writable.
2. Create the case folders with `New-CaseFolder` from the [PowerShell page](powershell.qmd#shouldprocess), and put the evidence in the host's `Evidence` folder. Hash it on arrival with `Get-FileInventory`.
3. Run tools against `Evidence`, writing to `Cases\<case>\Output`. Keep each tool's console log or log file in `Output`.
4. Before power-off, confirm the output is on the `Cases` share: `Get-FileInventory -Path <case>\Output | Export-Csv <case>\Notes\OutputInventory.csv -NoTypeInformation`.
5. Power off. Everything on the system disk is discarded; the next case starts clean.
